intent: Initial geometry proposal with a balanced sensor array and moderate size and mass to provide stable, generalizable line detection and control. Chose 5 sensors spaced symmetrically across the front to cover the track width well, with medium sensor size for good resolution and noise robustness. Wheel radius and track set for stable turning and speed. Expect this to provide good line detection and control balance on both oval and s-bend tracks, supporting the integrator's controller development.
learning: Next iteration, analyze telemetry for line loss events and rms error to adjust sensor positions or sizes if line detection is weak or noisy. Also monitor steering oscillation to tune sensor layout for smoother control.
rationale: With no prior telemetry, I designed a moderate-sized robot with 5 sensors spaced evenly across the front to maximize line detection coverage and symmetry, which should help the controller maintain line position on varied track shapes. The sensor size is medium (0.012) to balance resolution and noise robustness. The body dimensions and mass are moderate to ensure stability without excessive inertia. Wheel radius and track width are chosen to allow stable turning and speed. This geometry aims to generalize well across the development tracks and unseen tracks, providing a solid platform for the integrator. The requested measurements focus on completion, progress, rms_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation to evaluate line following performance and control smoothness.
